questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Plasma and Formed Elements' refers to.
questions.a: Blood is a specialized fluid connective tissue consisting of a liquid extracellular matrix termed plasma and suspended cellular components called formed elements.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Plasma and Formed Elements'.
questions.a: Plasma carries water, minerals, and essential proteins, while formed elements carry out gas transport, immunity, and blood clotting.

Explain in your own words what 'ABO and Rh Blood Grouping System' refers to.
questions.a: Classification system for human blood based on specific inherited surface antigens A, B, and Rh factor on red blood cells, along with plasma antibodies.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'ABO and Rh Blood Grouping System'.
questions.a: Transfusion compatibility depends on matching RBC surface antigens to prevent immune-mediated clumping and hemolysis.

Explain in your own words what 'Mechanism of Blood Coagulation' refers to.
questions.a: A multi-step enzymatic cascade reaction that converts liquid blood into an insoluble fibrin meshwork to prevent excessive blood loss upon vascular injury.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Mechanism of Blood Coagulation'.
questions.a: Platelets and tissue factors trigger a cascade converting inactive prothrombin into thrombin, which turns soluble fibrinogen into an insoluble fibrin clot.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Mechanism of Blood Coagulation', in plain ASCII form.

Explain in your own words what 'Lymph and Tissue Fluid' refers to.
questions.a: Fluid filtered from blood capillaries into tissue intercellular spaces that drains into the lymphatic system to return nutrients, proteins, and lymphocytes back to circulation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Lymph and Tissue Fluid'.
questions.a: Lymph acts as a middleman for exchange between blood and cells, carrying nutrients, hormones, absorbed fats, and defensive white blood cells.

concepts.title: Human Heart Structure and Nodal Conducting System

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Human Heart Structure and Nodal Conducting System' refers to.
questions.a: A four-chambered myogenic muscular organ featuring an internal autoexcitable conducting network composed of SAN, AVN, AV bundle, and Purkinje fibers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Human Heart Structure and Nodal Conducting System'.
questions.a: The sino-atrial node spontaneously fires action potentials to set the pace of rhythmic cardiac contractions.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Human Heart Structure and Nodal Conducting System', in plain ASCII form.

Explain in your own words what 'Cardiac Output Calculation' refers to.
questions.a: How much blood each ventricle pumps out in one minute, obtained as heart rate times the stroke volume.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cardiac Output Calculation'.
questions.a: Cardiac output measures heart performance and equals the product of volume per beat and beats per minute.

Explain in your own words what 'Duration of Cardiac Cycle' refers to.
questions.a: The elapsed time for one complete sequence of atrial and ventricular both systole and diastole, calculated by dividing sixty seconds by the heart rate.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Duration of Cardiac Cycle'.
questions.a: The total time duration of a single cardiac cycle varies in inverse proportion with the heart rate.

Explain in your own words what 'Electrocardiogram (ECG)' refers to.
questions.a: A standard electrical trace recording cardiac cycle depolarization and repolarization waves across P-wave, QRS complex, and T-wave segments.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Electrocardiogram (ECG)'.
questions.a: ECG waves represent distinct electrical events in the cardiac cycle used to evaluate heart health.

Explain in your own words what 'Double Circulation and Hepatic Portal System' refers to.
questions.a: The dual circulatory architecture comprising pulmonary circuit (heart-lungs-heart) and systemic circuit (heart-body-heart), along with specialized portal systems.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Double Circulation and Hepatic Portal System'.
questions.a: Double circulation ensures strict separation of both oxygenated and deoxygenated blood to optimize oxygen delivery.

Explain in your own words what 'Regulation of Cardiac Activity and Circulatory Disorders' refers to.
questions.a: Intrinsic myogenic control of heart rhythm modulated by autonomic neural both signals and hormones, alongside pathologies affecting blood pressure and coronary perfusion.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Regulation of Cardiac Activity and Circulatory Disorders'.
questions.a: Autonomic nerves and hormones modulate cardiac output, while vascular arterial blockages produce hypertension, CAD, angina, and heart failure.
